name: Any Language, One Can (the polyglot host)
one_liner: A judge orders one of the cans on the table in their own language; the G1 hears it natively with Gemma 4 (no speech recognizer), confirms in that language, walks to the table, takes the right can, walks back to whoever raised their hand and hands it over, with nothing leaving the robot.
story: My mother-in-law Yuki visited from Osaka last Thanksgiving. Thirty people, a table full of drinks, and she sat in the corner for two hours, because asking for a Coke in a language you do not have is harder than being thirsty. [beat] This is a Unitree G1. Its brain is one model, Gemma 4 E2B, two billion parameters, running on the Jetson in its chest. Nothing in this room has an internet connection: here is the unplugged cable, here is the phone in airplane mode. The same model hears you in your language, no speech recognizer in between, looks at the table, decides which can you meant, and calls one function: order. Our code does what code is good at: walking, aligning, closing a hand, not dropping you. [beat] Watch the screen: every decision shows up there with its latency, about a second to understand you, about 300 milliseconds per look. Every call this week is logged; the table on the slide is Thursday's thirty-run table, misses included, because when it misses it tells you and asks for help. The person holding the remote is a safety spotter; he never drives. [beat] Who wants a drink? Any language.
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (about 4 min per judge group, repeatable all day). 0:00 Judges arrive at a 3x3 m taped area. A laptop shows the live head-camera frame, the Gemma call log with per-call latency, and the state machine. Three different cans stand in a rack at the robot's hand height on a table 2.5 m away; the robot stands at its home mark. Teammate: 'Pick up the stick, press the button, order one of those three in any language.' 0:20 Judge: 'Dame la lata verde, por favor.' LED blue while listening, purple while Gemma thinks (about 1.2 s). The robot turns toward the voice (ReSpeaker direction of arrival) and answers in Spanish, 'La lata verde. Voy.' The dashboard shows order(item=green_can, language=es) and the latency. 0:35 It walks (0.4 m/s Move pulses, re-finding the rack with box_2d every ~0.8 s), stops at 0.35 m on lidar, aligns laterally, plays the recorded reach for that slot, closes the BrainCo hand to 0.7, lifts. Gate: 'Is the hand holding a can?' -> yes (one word, shown on screen). 1:10 It turns, asks 'Quien la pidio? Levanta la mano', finds the raised hand with box_2d, walks to 0.8 m, extends the arm to the handover pose; the release gate ('Is a human hand holding the can? yes/no' at ~3 Hz) opens the fingers when the judge takes it. 'Que la disfrutes.' Judges see the gate decide, not a timer. 1:40 VISIBLE FAILURE-RECOVERY: second judge orders in another language; the grasp gate returns no (it happens, and if it does not we nudge the rack): the robot says 'I missed it, one more try', re-aligns and retries; if the retry also fails it says 'I cannot reach it; would you put it in my hand?', opens the hand toward the judge, closes when the gate sees a can in the hand, and still delivers to the requester. 2:30 Numbers board: Orin latencies per call type, language table (n per language, order() correctness), grasp success over the last 30 trials, release-gate accuracy, battery. Optional: 'Or order from the phone: the same Gemma 4 model on the Tensor chip through LiteRT-LM; the phone only sends order() over our own Wi-Fi.' Reset ~40 s (refill rack, robot walks home). STAGE (2:45). 0:00-0:30 the Yuki story, the unplugged cable, one architecture slide. 0:30-1:00 a Gemma-team judge takes the stick and orders in their language; the robot confirms in that language (gasp 1: a humanoid answering in Hindi or Portuguese with no internet). 1:00-2:00 walk, grasp, return to the raised hand, handover (gasp 2); the projector shows the dashboard so 100 people watch the loop and the latencies. 2:00-2:30 second order from the phone if the Pixel track survived, else from a second judge; the recovery line is rehearsed as part of the show if anything misses. 2:30-2:45 numbers slide and the honest sentence: scripted skills, Gemma decisions, zero teleop. Plan B for a stage with steps: perform on the floor in front of the stage with the dashboard projected.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B (unsloth gemma-4-E2B-it-qat UD-Q4_K_XL + mmproj-BF16, which carries the gemma4a audio encoder) served by llama.cpp CUDA (arch 87) on PC2, one server, one slot, thinking off, greedy, cached system prefix per request type. Four request types: (1) ORDER: parts in the order image (480x336 frame of the rack, 70 tokens) -> short instruction -> input_audio (PTT clip <= 8 s, <= 200 audio tokens at 25 tok/s), with one tool order(item: enum of the 3-4 cans on the rack, language: enum of verified languages); Gemma hears the request in any language, matches it to what it sees, and emits one call (~500 prompt tokens, 15-20 output tokens). (2) LOCATE: box_2d of the requested can and of the person with a raised hand, using the harness's box-prefill format at 720x480 (150 tokens) for the table scene because 70 tokens misses objects in clutter. (3) GATES: one-word yes/no after the image ('Is the hand holding a can?', 'Is a human hand holding the can?', 'Is anyone raising a hand?'). (4) SPEAK: templated confirmation lines per verified language; for an unverified language Gemma writes a <= 12 word reply in the language of the audio. E4B (google QAT Q4_0, already cached) is held in reserve for the ORDER turn only if Tuesday's language table shows E2B under 8/10 on a target language and memory allows. Why Gemma is essential: one 2B model hears (no ASR), understands across languages, grounds the request in pixels, and emits a native function call; replace it with a text LLM and you need an ASR, a detector, and a translator, and the loop stops being sub-second.
litert_role: A judge-visible front end running Gemma 4 E2B through LiteRT-LM, in the loop as the close-talk 'ear' for a loud room. Primary: Pixel 11 app forked from litert-samples sample_app_tpu (litertlm-android 0.18.0, gemma-4-E2B-it_Google_Tensor_G6.litertlm with GPU/CPU fallback, Content.AudioFile 16 kHz mono WAV, ToolSet with the same <= 2-argument order(item, language) tool, automatic tool calling off, client-side validation, a warm-up generation at launch); the phone shows the live rack photo and sends order() as JSON over WebSocket to PC2 (mDNS/NsdManager, phone in airplane mode on our USB AP). Alternative if no Android developer joins: a Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB order kiosk with litert-lm-api (Engine(backend=cpu, audio_backend=cpu), USB mic, 7-inch display), Google's own Reachy-on-Pi precedent. Not used on the robot: LiteRT-LM has no CUDA path and its WebGPU backend is unsupported on Jetson; llama.cpp stays the sub-second perception engine. The robot's own stick-mic path works without the phone, so the LiteRT device is additive, never a single point of failure.
architecture: Devices: G1 PC2 (Orin NX 16 GB, JetPack 6.2) runs everything that touches the robot; a laptop on the owner's MT7612U USB AP (10.42.0.1) only renders the dashboard; optional Pixel 11 or Pi 5 on the same AP. No WAN anywhere; DDS stays on eth0. PC2 processes: llama-server (--jinja -np 1 --cache-ram 0 -c 4096 --swa-full, E2B + mmproj, ~4-5 GB GPU); brain.py state machine IDLE -> LISTEN -> UNDERSTAND -> CONFIRM -> APPROACH -> ALIGN -> GRASP -> VERIFY -> RETURN -> HANDOVER -> RECOVER; skills over unitree_sdk2py: loco (LocoClient GetFsmId==500 check, Move(vx,vy,vyaw) 1 s pulses, StopMove), arm (G1ArmActionClient.ExecuteAction 27 shake-hand or a recorded handover pose; per-slot reach trajectories on rt/arm_sdk at 50 Hz, kp 60/kd 1.5), hand (rt/brainco/right/cmd six floats, close 0.7, open 0.0), speak (Piper on CPU -> 16 kHz mono int16 -> AudioClient.PlayStream in 50 ms chunks, or a USB speaker via ALSA for the hall), led (AudioClient.LedControl, >= 200 ms apart), camera (pyrealsense2 640x480 after mscli stops video_hub_pc4; JPEG q85 at 480x336 or 720x480), lidar guard (rt/utlidar/cloud_livox_mid, front +-30 deg min range), odometry (rt/odommodestate) for the turn-around and home return, listen (ReSpeaker XVF3800 on the chest for DOA + DJI Mic Mini receiver as the handheld stick, PTT arcade button via evdev, webrtcvad end-pointing, 10 s cap), bridge (WebSocket server for the phone/Pi). Data flow per order: clip -> ORDER request -> order() -> template line -> Piper -> speaker; then a perceive-act loop at ~1 Hz (box_2d -> bearing/size -> Move pulse) until lidar standoff; align; reach; close; VERIFY gate; turn; raised-hand box_2d loop; handover pose; release gate at ~3 Hz. Expected on the Orin (harness projections plus the Orin Nano Super audio report, all to be measured Monday): one-word gate 0.25-0.45 s; box_2d 0.65-0.9 s; ORDER turn 1.0-1.5 s (TTFT 0.4-0.6 s + ~20 tokens at ~27 ms); Piper 0.2-0.4 s per sentence; speech-end to robot reply ~1.5-2 s; walk 2.5 m ~8 s; grasp 6-8 s; whole loop ~60 s. Memory: E2B + mmproj + KV ~5 GB GPU, Piper + skills + camera ~1.5 GB, headroom for a second model is there but not needed. Dashboard: MJPEG + JSON over the AP, every model call with ms.

why_it_wins: It is the Figure-01 apple moment with a twist judges have not seen: the order arrives in the judge's own language and the model that hears it is the model that sees the table and calls the function, with no cloud and no ASR. The physical act is unmistakable and complete (walk, take, return, hand over), the participatory moment is in the judge's language, and the recovery is designed to be shown. The numbers board (per-call Orin latencies, language table, 30-trial grasp and release rates) answers the 'is it real' question before it is asked, and the tiered grasp means the stage never depends on the one unproven primitive.

fallback: Tier B point-and-pass: the robot still hears the order in any language, confirms in that language, walks to the table, points at the right can (body turn to its box_2d bearing plus the 'right hand up' preset or a recorded point pose) and asks the judge to place it in its open hand; the hand closes when the gate sees a can in it, then it walks back and hands over. The loop, the language and the walk survive; the slide says 'grasp: human-assisted'. If walking is gated: a stationary host at a bar table. If Orin audio fails: sherpa-onnx ASR -> text into Gemma, declared on the slide. If the Pixel app fails: the Pi kiosk, or no side device at all.
angle: Stage-demo maximalist. Each concept is built backwards from the 2-3 minute moment on stage: one protagonist, one judge speaking to the robot in their own language, one unmistakable physical act, and a failure the robot recovers from out loud. Every concept is tiered so the Oct 23 rehearsal, not hope, decides which tier is shown. Gemma 4 E2B on the robot's own Orin NX is the only brain (native audio in, vision, native tool calls; no ASR, no detector, no translator in front of it); code owns sequencing and safety; every number on the slide is measured on the Orin; a human spotter holds L2+B and never drives. The three are deliberately different acts: a butler that fetches (object act), an apprentice that learns from one look (learning act), and a guide that leads by the hand (assistive locomotion act).

name: Show Me Once (the apprentice)
one_liner: A judge invents a three-move handshake and performs it once in front of the robot; Gemma 4 watches through the robot's own camera, names the moves in order, says them back in the judge's language, and the G1 performs the routine with them, high-five contact included, all on the Orin; it remembers whose routine is whose by name.
story: My nephew Theo is seven. He and his dad have a secret handshake, and the rule is that you have to be shown it, once, in person. Nobody has ever written it down. [beat] Robots today learn from millions of videos in a data center. Theo learned his from one look. So we asked: can a humanoid learn a routine from one person, once, with nothing but what it can see and hear, using a model that fits in its chest? [beat] This is Gemma 4 E2B on the G1's Jetson. No cloud: the cable is out, the Wi-Fi is our own box with no uplink. You press the button, say 'watch me' in your language, and show it three moves. It watches through its own eyes, names what it saw, says the sequence back in your language, and then does it with you, including the high five, which means it has to wait for your hand. What it learns is the sequence and how to map your body onto its own; the moves come from a vocabulary of fifteen it already knows. That sentence is on the slide, because that is exactly where this goes next: the vocabulary grows. [beat] And it remembers whose routine is whose, by name. Come back in an hour and ask for yours.
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (about 3 min per judge group). 0:00 Judges arrive; a laptop shows the live camera with the pose skeleton overlay (LiteRT MediaPipe), the keyframes as they are cut, the Gemma call log with latencies, and the state. A menu card lists the ten moves it can do (high five, clap, heart, hands up, wave, hug, point, X, shake hand, bow-as-hands-up). Teammate: 'Press the button, say watch me in your language, then show it three moves, slowly.' 0:15 Judge: 'Regarde-moi.' LED blue. The judge performs high five, heart, wave. On screen: wrist-speed minima cut three keyframes; each gets a one-word label from Gemma (0.3-0.45 s each), then one six-frame sequence request returns perform(steps=[high_five, heart, wave]) as a cross-check. 0:40 Robot, in French: 'Compris: high five, coeur, salut. Pret?' Judge: 'Vas-y.' PERFORM: for the high five the robot raises its hand (ExecuteAction 18) and holds until the sync gate ('Is the person holding a palm up? yes/no') says yes, then completes the tap (contact, the gasp), then heart (20), then high wave (26). 1:15 'Souviens-toi: c est la poignee de main de Claire' -> remember(name=Claire) stored on the robot; the dashboard shows the stored sequence. 1:30 VISIBLE FAILURE-RECOVERY: a second judge includes a move outside the vocabulary (a bow or a fist bump); the sequence call returns unknown for that step and the robot says 'I do not have that move yet; the closest I can do is hands up. Use it?' The judge says yes or no (heard by Gemma in their language), the robot performs the adjusted routine. If keyframing miscounts, it says 'I saw two moves; show me the last one again' and re-watches only that one. 2:15 Numbers board: per-move label accuracy (n), three-move sequence accuracy, keyframe precision/recall, latencies on the Orin, how many strangers' routines it learned today and the recall success rate. 2:30 if the stretch tier passed Wednesday's gate: 'Show it a chore': the judge slides the red cup from the left mat to the right mat; the robot says 'You moved the red cup to the right mat' and replays it with a push-slide sweep. STAGE (2:45). 0:00-0:30 the Theo story, the unplugged cable, the one honest sentence about vocabulary. 0:30-1:15 a Gemma-team judge invents a handshake and shows it once, in their language. 1:15-2:00 the robot names it back in that language and performs it with them, waiting for the hand on the high five (the room's phones come out here). 2:00-2:30 'Who taught it something earlier today?' A judge from the bench rounds says their name; the robot recalls and performs their routine. 2:30-2:45 numbers slide; if the chore tier is live, the cup slide replaces the recall.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B (same cached GGUF + mmproj) via llama.cpp CUDA on PC2, thinking off, greedy. (1) WATCH: 3-8 keyframes at 480x336 (70 tokens each) sent as a 1 fps frame sequence with the question after the frames: 'List the gestures the person performed, in order' -> native tool call perform(steps=[enum of 10 moves + unknown]), <= 30 output tokens; cross-checked by the harness's proven format, a one-word label per keyframe ('Which gesture: high_five, clap, heart, hands_up, wave, hug, point, x, shake_hand, none?'). The per-keyframe path is the fallback if sequence listing proves unreliable (the harness showed E2B composes poorly without thinking, but listing observed gestures is perception, not planning; it is a day-1 measurement). (2) HEAR: PTT clip (<= 6 s, <= 150 audio tokens) -> teach(name), watch(), recall(name), go() tool calls; Gemma hears 'watch me' in any language and the reply is templated per verified language, with Gemma writing a short line for others. (3) SYNC: one-word gates during the performance ('Is the person holding a palm up for a high five?') so contact moves wait for the human. Why Gemma is essential: frames-to-sequence is grounded multi-image understanding plus function calling, and the hearing is native; a text LLM would need a gesture classifier, an ASR and a translator, while here one 2B model does all three from pixels and PCM.
litert_role: LiteRT, the runtime (ai-edge-litert aarch64 wheel, CPU/XNNPACK on the Orin), runs MediaPipe Pose Landmarker lite and Hand Landmarker at ~30 fps on the head camera to track the wrists, cut keyframes at motion minima (SeeDo-style) and detect the raised palm for the sync gate; it is visibly in the loop as the skeleton overlay on the dashboard. LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 E2B is added only if Monday's GPU test passes on PC2 (prebuilt/linux_arm64 on LD_LIBRARY_PATH): it would then host the WATCH turn so the llama.cpp slot stays free for the live sync gates. Honest caveat on the slide: the prize text says 'use LiteRT-LM'; MediaPipe-on-LiteRT alone is a partial claim and is presented as such, with no side device added just to chase the pool.
architecture: Devices: G1 PC2 only, plus a dashboard laptop on the USB AP; no WAN, DDS on eth0. PC2 processes: llama-server (E2B, one slot, harness flags); mediapipe/LiteRT landmarkers at 30 fps on CPU; brain.py state machine IDLE -> LISTEN -> WATCH -> LABEL -> CONFIRM -> PERFORM -> REMEMBER -> RECOVER; skills over unitree_sdk2py: gesture (G1ArmActionClient.ExecuteAction ids 18 high five, 17 clap, 20 heart, 15 hands up, 26 high wave, 25 face wave, 19 hug, 23 right hand up, 22 X, 27 shake hand, 99 release; LocoClient.WaveHand/ShakeHand as alternates; recorded rt/arm_sdk trajectories at 50 Hz as the fallback library), speak (Piper -> AudioClient.PlayStream or USB speaker), led (LedControl), camera (pyrealsense2 640x480 at 15 fps -> landmarker; 480x336 JPEG crops to Gemma), listen (DJI Mic Mini receiver or ReSpeaker via ALSA, PTT button via evdev, webrtcvad), memory (JSON name -> steps on PC2). Stretch chore tier: rt/arm_sdk sweep at table height with lateral alignment from box_2d on the cup. Data flow: PTT clip -> HEAR -> watch() -> landmarker keyframes -> LABEL (one-word per keyframe, 0.25-0.45 s each on the Orin, or one 6-frame sequence call ~1.2-1.8 s) -> perform() -> template line -> Piper -> speaker -> presets with sync gates (0.3-0.45 s each) -> remember(). Expected on the Orin: keyframing real time; watch-to-confirm pause ~2-3 s, filled by LED and a 'let me think' line; audio intent turn 1.0-1.5 s; Piper 0.3 s; each preset 2-4 s. Memory: E2B ~4-5 GB GPU, landmarkers ~0.3 GB, headroom for a LiteRT-LM GPU engine if it runs.

name: Lantern (a humanoid guide that narrates the world)
one_liner: A blindfolded judge holds a breakaway handle in the robot's hand and says where they want to go in their language; Gemma 4 hears it, finds the target with the robot's eyes, and the G1 walks them there at a careful pace, narrating what is ahead in their language and stopping, out loud, when someone crosses, with zero cloud and a second Gemma model remembering what it saw that morning.
story: Marco lost his sight at forty-one. A guide dog takes two years and about fifty thousand dollars to train, and even the best one cannot tell him that the coffee is on the left or what the sign on the door says. [beat] This is Lantern: a humanoid that takes your hand, hears where you want to go in your language, finds it with its own eyes, walks you there at a careful pace, and tells you what is ahead, in your language, the whole way. The brain is Gemma 4 E2B on the Jetson in its chest. Nothing phones home: this cable is unplugged, the Wi-Fi is our own box with no uplink. [beat] Watch what happens when someone crosses our path: it stops, says so, and waits. That is not a glitch, that is the product. It also remembers the room: it walked this floor this morning and stored what it saw with a second Gemma model, EmbeddingGemma 2, so you can ask for things it cannot see from here. [beat] This is not a guide dog and we will not pretend it is: it is six days of work and a 35 kg robot with a spotter on the e-stop and a handle that lets go before you do. But it is the first time any of us has seen a humanoid describe a room to someone in Portuguese with no server behind it. Who wants to close their eyes?
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (about 3.5 min per judge group; the blindfold is the judge's choice at the bench). 0:00 A 4 m lane is taped on the floor with two landmarks: a red chair and a 'coffee' sign on a stand. The laptop shows the live frame with boxes, the path-clear verdict, the sentence being spoken, and the call log with latencies. Teammate: 'Hold the handle like a suitcase, press the button on it, and tell it where you want to go, in your language.' 0:15 Judge: 'Leva-me ate a cadeira vermelha.' LED blue, then purple ~1.2 s; guide_to(target=red chair, language=pt) appears; the robot, in Portuguese: 'Vamos. A cadeira vermelha esta a quatro metros, em frente, a esquerda.' 0:30 It walks at 0.3 m/s in 1 s Move pulses, steering on the chair's box_2d bearing (0.7-0.9 s per frame), lidar front sector as the hard stop; every ~3 s a one-sentence narration in Portuguese from the current frame ('Mesa a direita, caminho livre'). 0:55 VISIBLE FAILURE-RECOVERY: a teammate (later, judges do it themselves) crosses the lane; the path-clear gate (one word every ~0.5 s) flips to no and the lidar confirms: the robot stops within one pulse and says 'Alguem esta a passar. Esperamos.' then resumes when both say clear. 1:25 Arrival: it stops 0.8 m short, turns the person square to the chair using the box geometry, and says 'A cadeira esta mesmo a sua frente, um passo.' The judge says 'obrigado' and the robot opens its hand to release the handle on the word, not on a timer. 1:50 Memory question: 'Onde viste o cafe esta manha?' -> EmbeddingGemma 2 retrieval over the morning walk-through -> 'Perto da janela, uns seis metros atras de nos. Vamos?' -> odometry-guided walk to that pose, then live box_2d on the sign. 2:40 Numbers board: hear/steer/gate/narration latencies on the Orin, path-clear gate accuracy with crossings (n), language table, 20-run guided-walk success, handle pull-out force and breakaway threshold, memory retrieval top-1 rate. STAGE (2:45). 0:00-0:30 the Marco story, the unplugged cable, the honest 'not a guide dog' line. 0:30-1:00 a Gemma-team judge is blindfolded (a teammate if the organizers prefer), takes the handle, asks in their language; the robot answers in it. 1:00-2:15 the walk across the floor with narration; a planned stranger crosses; stop, announcement, resume (the gasp is the stop). 2:15-2:45 arrival, release on the word, 'take me back to where we started' by odometry, numbers slide.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B (cached GGUF + mmproj-BF16) via llama.cpp CUDA on PC2, thinking off, greedy, cached system prefix per request type. HEAR: PTT clip from the handle mic (<= 6 s) -> guide_to(target: short string, language: enum) in ~1.0-1.5 s. SEE: box_2d of the target with the harness's prefill format at 720x480 (150 tokens, 0.7-0.9 s) -> bearing and apparent size -> steering and standoff. GATE: one word 'Is the path directly ahead clear of people and objects? yes or no' every ~0.5 s at 480x336 (0.25-0.45 s), fused with the lidar front sector; the gate also confirms arrival and the 'person still beside me' check. NARRATE: 'In one short <language> sentence, say what is ahead' (<= 20 tokens, ~1 s) every ~3 s while walking; arrival phrasing is templated from box geometry ('one step ahead, slightly left'). The language of all speech is the language Gemma identified in the request. EmbeddingGemma 2 (Gemma family, Oct 6) provides the venue memory through LiteRT-LM. Why Gemma is essential: one model hears the destination in the user's language, grounds it in pixels, and writes the narration in that language; remove it and you need an ASR, an open-vocabulary detector, a captioner and a translator, and none of that fits the Orin at these latencies.
litert_role: LiteRT-LM 0.18 on PC2 (CPU, pip wheels, Python 3.10) runs EmbeddingGemma 2 via litert-lm serve (/v1/embeddings). During a 5 min morning walk-through driven by the remote, the robot stores every 2 s a record {E2B one-sentence caption, EmbeddingGemma 2 embedding of the caption (and of the frame if the serve endpoint accepts image parts; else text only), odometry pose from rt/odommodestate}. At ask time the request is embedded, the top-1 record's pose becomes the goal, the robot walks by odometry in straight lidar-guarded segments (<= 6 m), then hands over to live box_2d. Judge-visible: 'ask it for anything it saw this morning', and the retrieval hit is shown on the dashboard. The memory path is CPU by design (embeddings are tens of milliseconds); LiteRT-LM GPU on Jetson is unsupported and is not relied on. An optional Pixel 11 narrator app (Gemma 4 E2B via LiteRT-LM on the phone reading the robot's frames into an earpiece) is listed only if a mobile developer joins; it is not in the baseline.
architecture: Devices: G1 PC2 for everything on the robot; dashboard laptop on the USB AP; no WAN, DDS on eth0. PC2 processes: llama-server (E2B, one slot, harness flags); litert-lm serve with EmbeddingGemma 2 (CPU); brain.py state machine IDLE -> LISTEN -> RESOLVE (in sight via box_2d, else memory) -> WALK (0.3 m/s LocoClient.Move pulses; steering from bearing; stop on lidar front +-30 deg < 0.6 m or gate = no; narration every 3 s) -> ARRIVE -> RELEASE -> RECOVER. Skills over unitree_sdk2py: loco (GetFsmId == 500, Move, StopMove), hand (left BrainCo rt/brainco/left/cmd closes to 0.9 on the handle bar, opens on the release word), speak (Piper en/es/pt/fr/de/it/zh -> AudioClient.PlayStream or USB speaker), led (LedControl: blue listening, purple thinking, green walking, red stopped), camera (D435i via pyrealsense2 after stopping video_hub_pc4), lidar (rt/utlidar/cloud_livox_mid), odometry (rt/odommodestate), listen (lavalier transmitter and PTT button mounted on the handle; ReSpeaker on the chest as backup). Handle: 300 mm bar in the robot's closed hand, a loop strap for the human, a magnetic breakaway rated under ~2 kg so a stumble on either side separates them; a USB cable runs the button and the mic receiver to PC2. Expected on the Orin: hear 1.0-1.5 s; one steering decision per 1 s pulse (box_2d 0.7-0.9 s); gate 0.25-0.45 s; narration ~1 s plus Piper 0.3 s; retrieval < 50 ms; a 4 m guided walk ~15-20 s with narration. Memory: E2B ~5 GB GPU, EmbeddingGemma 2 < 1 GB CPU, Piper and skills ~1 GB.

name: Any-Language Butler
one_liner: A Unitree G1 that hears a request in any language, confirms what it saw and heard, walks to a side table, picks up the can and hands it over, with every byte of inference on its own Jetson.
story: "Ask it in your own language." A judge from the crowd says 'tráeme la lata roja' into the mic. One second later the robot's LED turns green and it answers, in English and in Spanish, 'the red can on the table, to your right, got it' because one Gemma 4 E2B model heard the audio natively, looked through the head camera and emitted a single tool call. It walks three meters to the table, stops when the LiDAR says it is close enough, finds the can in the frame with a 378 ms box detection, closes its BrainCo hand, comes back and holds the can out until it feels the judge take it. No wake word service, no Whisper, no cloud: the Wi-Fi light on the router is the only network, and we unplug the uplink on stage. Behind it, LiteRT-LM runs EmbeddingGemma 2 as the robot's memory: ask 'what did the last person ask you for?' and it searches what it heard and saw. We show our success-rate table (n trials, per-language) and let it fail once on purpose: hide the can and it says 'I don't see a can; can you put it back?' and tries again. The pitch is honest: one small open model, a 35 kg body, measured latencies on the slide, and a loop that beats Google's own Reachy Mini reference by hearing without an STT.
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (repeat every 5-6 min, battery on charger between rounds, robot standing at a taped mark 3 m from a 75 cm table with 3 cans): 0:00 presenter points at the travel router: 'that is the whole network, uplink unplugged'. 0:15 PARTICIPATORY: judge presses the hold-to-talk arcade button (or wears the lavalier) and asks in any language for one of the cans; LED blue = listening. 0:17 LED amber; within ~1.5 s robot speaks back what it understood in English + the judge's language (Piper TTS; fixed lines pre-rendered), display on the laptop shows the raw tool call JSON and the latency. 0:25 robot turns toward the table (box_2d bearing), walks in 1 s Move pulses, LiDAR min-range guard stops it at 0.6 m. 0:45 head camera box detection on the requested can (140-280 image tokens for the table scene), recorded arm_sdk reach trajectory for that tray slot, BrainCo close to ~0.7, lift, vision check 'is there a can in my right hand? yes/no' (222 ms class). 1:10 walk back toward the judge (DOA angle from rt/audio_msg or person box), extend arm (shake-hand pose id 27), open hand when the BrainCo finger-position state shows the can being pulled / after the judge says 'thanks'. 1:30 FAILURE-RECOVERY (every round): presenter hides the can under a cloth before the second request; robot answers 'I don't see the red can' (4-way answer with none), asks, cloth removed, retries successfully. 1:50 memory question to LiteRT-LM/EmbeddingGemma 2: 'what did the previous judge ask for?' 2:10 success-rate table and the latency breakdown slide. STAGE (2.5 min): same loop once, presenter narrates the protagonist (a wheelchair user asking from across the room), uplink cable held up and unplugged on camera, one deliberate failure+recovery, backup video on the laptop in case of a fall.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B (unsloth QAT UD-Q4_K_XL + mmproj-BF16, the exact files cached on the Mac) on PC2 via llama.cpp CUDA sm_87, --jinja -np 1 -c 4096 --swa-full --cache-ram 0, thinking off, greedy. Three request types, all direct questions placed after the media: (a) VOICE: [480x336 frame][text 'The user spoke. Call one tool.'][input_audio <=10 s, 16 kHz mono, <=250 audio tokens] -> native tool call fetch(object, color) | come_here() | gesture(name) | answer(text, language); (b) BEARING: box_2d assistant-prefill detection of the fridge/table/can (100% at 378 ms on the Mac); (c) CHECKS: one-word yes/no ('is there a can in my right hand?', 'is a person within 1 m?'). Audio is why Gemma is essential: no STT stage, the model transcribes, understands, picks the reply language and chooses the tool in one pass (verified on the Mac in 232-511 ms for spoken commands). Geometry and sequencing live in a Python state machine because thinking-off E2B cannot compose plans from an image. name: Pixel Is the Brain
one_liner: A Pixel 11 strapped to the G1's chest runs Gemma 4 E2B on the Tensor G6 via LiteRT-LM as the humanoid's ears, eyes, face and planner, and ships tiny tool calls over Wi-Fi to the Jetson, which does sub-second perception and the skills.
story: "The phone in your pocket can be the mind of a humanoid." A judge taps the big microphone button on the phone mounted on the robot's chest and speaks in Korean. The phone shows what it heard, what it sees through its own camera, and the one-line decision it made, 'fetch(object=can, color=red)', all computed on the Pixel's TPU with Gemma 4 E2B through LiteRT-LM, in airplane mode. The robot answers in Korean through the phone speaker, walks to the table, and the Jetson's own Gemma 4 instance, the fast perception loop we measured at 378 ms, guides the hand to the can. The phone is not a remote control; it is the protagonist: it hears, sees, plans, speaks, remembers, and shows its reasoning trail to anyone passing the bench. Two Gemmas, two chips, one Android app, zero cloud. The pitch to Android judges: an end-to-end Pixel AI experience whose output is a 35 kg body doing a chore; the pitch to robotics judges: the most transparent, auditable humanoid loop in the room, because every decision is on a screen.
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (5-6 min): 0:00 judge sees the Pixel 11 on the chest mount in airplane mode (Wi-Fi only to our travel router); presenter: 'everything you see is computed on this phone and that Jetson'. 0:10 PARTICIPATORY: judge holds the phone's mic button and speaks in any language (phone mics are far better than the robot's array); screen shows the live transcript, the camera frame the model saw, and the JSON tool call with the on-phone latency. 0:20 the phone speaks back in the judge's language (Android TextToSpeech offline voice), robot LED turns green. 0:30 app sends fetch(...) over WebSocket to PC2; robot turns, walks to the table with the Jetson Gemma bearing loop, LiDAR stop. 0:50 Jetson box detection on the can, recorded reach, BrainCo close, vision check, lift. 1:15 return toward the judge (person box bearing from the head camera), shake-hand pose, release on grip-state change. 1:35 FAILURE-RECOVERY: judge asks for an object not on the table; the phone's Gemma answers 'I don't see a yellow can; I see red, blue and green. Which one?' (constrained JSON with an alternatives list) and waits; judge picks one; loop completes. 2:00 judge scrolls the phone's decision log (audit trail of every request, call and latency) and asks 'what did the person before me ask?' (EmbeddingGemma 2 memory on the phone via LiteRT-LM). 2:30 numbers slide: on-phone end-to-end voice->tool call, Jetson perception latencies, success table (no TPU tok/s on the slide, per Tensor ML terms). STAGE (2.5 min): same loop, phone screen mirrored to the projector over our router (scrcpy from the laptop, local), airplane mode shown to the camera, one deliberate failure, backup video ready.
gemma_role: Two instances, two chips. (1) Pixel 11: Gemma 4 E2B gemma-4-E2B-it_Google_Tensor_G6.litertlm (4-bit, 8192 ctx) through litertlm-android 0.18.0, forked from litert-samples/sample_app_tpu (Apache 2.0) with TPU->GPU->CPU fallback; inputs Content.AudioBytes (16 kHz mono 16-bit PCM, <=15 s) + Content.ImageBytes (one 480x336 CameraX frame, visualTokenBudget 70) + a short text; outputs via ToolSet @Tool functions with <=2 simple args: fetch(object, color), come_here(), gesture(name), say(text, language); ConversationConfig.enableResponseFormat + ResponseFormat JSON schema (LLGuidance) for the clarification turn; ThinkingConfig 0; automaticToolCalling off, validated client-side, warm-up generation at launch. Why essential: native audio understanding + language choice + tool emission in one pass on the phone, and the same model family grounding the robot. (2) PC2: Gemma 4 E2B via llama.cpp CUDA, the measured fast path (box_2d prefill at ~0.65-0.9 s projected, one-word checks ~0.3 s) for bearing, can detection, hand-check and person detection; thinking off, greedy. Token budgets: phone turn ~300 cached system+tools + 70 image + <=375 audio + <=25 output; Jetson turns as in the harness.
litert_role: LiteRT-LM is the primary cognitive runtime: Gemma 4 E2B on the Pixel TPU (NPU runtime com.google.ai.edge.litert:litert-npu-runtime-google-tensor:2.3.0, Backend NPU preference with GPU/CPU fallback logged on screen), audioBackend=CPU, visionBackend per day-1 timing; EmbeddingGemma 2 (Pixel 11 Pro TPU embeds text in ~8 ms) via litertlm-android for the on-phone memory of past requests and scene captions; ML Kit Speech Recognition Advanced mode as a bonus live-caption overlay only (not in the decision path, to keep Gemma the ear). On the Jetson, LiteRT-LM is not used (CUDA is faster for the perception loop); that is stated plainly on the slide.
architecture: Devices: Pixel 11 256 GB (12 GB RAM) in a chest mount, airplane mode + Wi-Fi to a GL.iNet travel router; G1 PC2 (Orin NX) with llama-server + skills; laptop only for scrcpy mirroring and the backup video. name: Show Me Once
one_liner: A judge demonstrates a two-step chore at the table; Gemma 4 watches through the G1's head camera, extracts the steps, says them back for confirmation, and the humanoid repeats the chore, with a Raspberry Pi 5 running LiteRT-LM as the on-bench coach that grounds the steps to the robot's skills.
story: "A robot that learns a chore from watching you once" is Google's own line for this event, and this is the open-model version of it. A judge walks up, moves the red can from the left tray to the right tray and gives a thumbs-up. The robot's LED pulses: Gemma 4 E2B on its Jetson has been looking at one frame per second, picked the frames where the hand moved, asked itself one plain question per frame ('which object is the hand holding, picking up or putting down?'), and then, in a single thinking turn, wrote the plan: pick(red can, left tray), place(right tray), gesture(thumbs-up). The coach station, a Raspberry Pi 5 running the same Gemma 4 family through LiteRT-LM, shows the keyframes and the plan, and maps each step to the robot's skill library by EmbeddingGemma 2 similarity, so 'put it over there' and 'drop it in the other tray' land on the same skill. The robot says 'you moved the red can to the right tray, then a thumbs-up, correct?'; the judge says 'yes' (or corrects it by voice, which the Pi hears natively); and the G1 does it, with a grip check from its own camera, and retries once if the can slips. No training, no teleop, no cloud: a video-understanding model, a skill library, and an honest confirmation step.
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (6 min): 0:00 setup visible: robot at a taped mark facing a 75 cm table with two trays, three cans; Pi 5 coach display beside the table; router only. 0:10 PARTICIPATORY: judge performs a 1-2 step chore in front of the robot (move a can between trays, optionally wave/clap/thumbs-up at the end), 10-20 s. 0:30 LED amber 'learning': Pi display shows the 3-5 keyframes as they are selected, each with Gemma's one-line percept (~0.5 s each on the Jetson), then the plan call (one thinking turn, 5-8 s, progress bar). 0:45 robot speaks the plan back and asks for confirmation; judge says yes/no into the Pi's USB mic (Gemma 4 via LiteRT-LM on the Pi, audio-in, 3-5 s) or presses the big button. 1:00 execution: reach the source tray (recorded arm_sdk trajectory), BrainCo close, vision check 'is there a can in my right hand?', move to the target tray, open, then the gesture via ExecuteAction (17 clap, 18 high five, 26 wave, 20 heart). 1:45 FAILURE-RECOVERY (scripted every round): presenter nudges the can during the second demo so the grip check fails; robot says 'I dropped it, trying once more', re-grasps; if the second try fails it says so and asks for help. 2:15 second judge tries a different chore order (right->left, different can); 3:00 the coach display shows the session log and the success table (chores understood / executed / recovered, n); 3:30 reset trays. STAGE (2.5 min): presenter (protagonist: a grandparent teaching a helper robot a kitchen routine) demonstrates once, the robot repeats, one failure+recovery, ending with the gesture it learned; uplink unplugged on camera; backup video ready.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B on PC2 (llama.cpp CUDA, thinking off for perception, greedy) in three roles: (a) KEYFRAME PERCEPTION: 1 fps 480x336 frames from the D435i (video is frames at 1 fps, 70 tokens/frame), keyframes chosen in code by frame-difference energy of the hand region (box_2d of 'the person's hand' every frame, 0.65-0.9 s projected), then one direct question per keyframe after the image: 'Which object is the hand holding, and is it picking it up, putting it down, or gesturing?' answered as a short constrained phrase (140-280 image tokens for table clutter, ~20 output tokens). (b) PLAN COMPOSITION: one call with thinking ON (budget ~256 tokens, 5-8 s projected on Orin) given only the text percepts in order, emitting a native tool call plan(steps=[...]) restricted to the skill catalog (pick, place, gesture, say); the harness shows text-only percept->plan works where image->plan does not, so the image never enters this call. (c) EXECUTION CHECKS: one-word yes/no ('is there a can in my right hand?', 'is the red can in the right tray?') at ~0.3 s. Why essential: a multimodal model that can read a human demonstration from frames and write a tool-call plan is the whole product; the audio-in path on the Pi handles the confirmation and corrections in any language. Token budgets: percept turns ~40 cached + 70-280 image + 25 question + 20 output; plan turn ~350 prompt + 256 thinking + 60 output.
litert_role: Raspberry Pi 5 16 GB 'coach station' with LiteRT-LM 0.18.0: (1) Gemma 4 E2B (litert-community gemma-4-E2B-it-litert-lm, CPU, ~99 prefill / 9 decode tok/s) takes the judge's spoken yes/no/correction through a USB mic as Content.AudioFile (<=8 s clips, audio_backend=cpu) and returns a constrained JSON {confirm|correct, replacement_step} via ResponseFormat + LL_GUIDANCE (3-5 s, off the robot's critical path; fallback Moonshine-tiny + text prompt if audio TTFT exceeds ~4 s); (2) EmbeddingGemma 2 via `litert-lm serve` /v1/embeddings grounds each free-text step from the plan to the nearest entry of the skill library (pick/place per tray, 15 gestures by name) with cosine similarity, which makes the plan robust to paraphrase and is visible on the display; (3) the Pi draws the keyframes/plan/log page (Chromium kiosk) and talks to PC2 over WebSocket on the travel-router LAN. On the Jetson, llama.cpp stays the engine for the sub-second frame loop; LiteRT-LM GPU on the Orin is tried on day 1 and, if it works, moves the plan-composition call there as a bonus.
architecture: Devices: G1 PC2 (Orin NX, llama-server one slot + Python state machine + skills), Pi 5 16 GB (LiteRT-LM Gemma 4 E2B + EmbeddingGemma 2 + kiosk display + USB mic + arcade button), GL.iNet travel router, laptop only for the backup video. Data flow: D435i 640x480 at 1 fps (pyrealsense2, video_hub_pc4 stopped) -> hand box + frame-diff keyframe selector (code) -> per-keyframe percept (Gemma, llama-server) -> percept list -> plan tool call (Gemma, thinking on) -> JSON to the Pi over WebSocket -> EmbeddingGemma skill grounding + display -> spoken confirmation via Piper on the Jetson through AudioClient.PlayStream (+ Pebble V3 USB speaker) -> judge reply via Pi mic/button -> executor on PC2: rt/arm_sdk 50 Hz recorded trajectories for 2 tray slots x (reach, lift, carry, lower), rt/brainco/right/cmd close 0.7 / open 0, rt/brainco/right/state grip check, G1ArmActionClient.ExecuteAction for gestures (then 99 release), LocoClient kept in FSM 500 standing (no walking in the core loop, which removes the locomotion risk), LedControl for states. Expected latencies: keyframe percepts 3-5 x 0.7 s, plan 5-8 s, Pi confirmation 3-5 s, execution 25-40 s, whole loop ~60-80 s. Memory on PC2 ~5.5 GB for llama-server with a 256-token thinking budget at -c 4096; Pi ~3 GB.

Best Use of LiteRT: LiteRT-LM on the Pi with audio-in and EmbeddingGemma 2 grounding is visible and two weeks new; P(top-3) ~0.25 -> EV ~$1.0k; weaker than concept 2 because the main loop is llama.cpp.

Qualcomm / Pixel / Best in Show: not targeted.
Portfolio EV ~$4.7k if stacking allowed, ~$3.3k otherwise; widest outcome spread (a flawless run is the room's best story; a broken plan step is the room's most awkward).
why_it_wins: It is the demo the organizers described in their own inspiration text and the one closest to the Gemma team's current zeitgeist (Argon cornhole, Robotics On-Device 2), done with an open 2B-effective model and no learning phase, so the judges' 'is it real' test is answered on the bench by letting any judge invent the chore. The confirmation step turns E2B's weakness (no reliable plan without a human check) into an auditable, non-hallucinatory design, which the Gemma winners posts explicitly praise. Participation is maximal: the judge is the teacher.

first_48h_spikes: Plan-extraction accuracy on the Mac with the 10 chore videos: keyframes -> percepts -> text-only plan call (thinking 256) scored against ground truth; this single number decides the concept by Tuesday night.
Orin: llama.cpp CUDA perception timings, thinking-on plan call wall time with a 256-token budget (projected 6-8 s), and 1 fps D435i capture on PC2 under JetPack 6.2 (USB3; USB2 hub fallback).
Arm reach + BrainCo grasp between two fixed trays on the stand, then floor with spotter; grip check reliability (vision yes/no + finger-state) over 20 grasps.
Pi 5: LiteRT-LM E2B audio-in confirmation latency for 3-8 s clips (fallback Moonshine + text), EmbeddingGemma 2 /v1/embeddings up, skill grounding on 30 paraphrases.
Gesture mirroring baseline (fallback) measured: Gemma classifies a judge's gesture from 3 frames into {wave, clap, high five, heart, thumbs-up, none} -> ExecuteAction; accuracy over 30 trials.
Audio/LED/speaker contention with the factory offline assistant while the mic is in wake mode (or keep the onboard mic off and use only the Pi mic).
risks: Learn-from-watching with an open small VLM is unproven (SeeDo's open baselines scored near zero); mitigated by the one-question-per-frame design, text-only composition, a tiny skill vocabulary, the confirmation step, and the gesture-mirroring fallback decided by Tuesday night.

Thinking-on plan call may exceed 8 s on the Orin or produce an empty content/looping output (E2B burns its budget); mitigated by a 256-token budget, greedy, and a fallback rule-based composer from percepts.
Table grasp/place reliability (medium-low feasibility) with two fixed slots; mitigated by recorded trajectories, light cans, and the retry-once + ask-for-help recovery.
The head camera has no pan/tilt (no head joints) and the demo area must stay in a fixed frame; the judge must demonstrate inside tape marks.
Pi audio in a loud house: push-button confirmation is the zero-risk path; Pi mic is a bonus.
Extra device (Pi) lowers P(works) and may be seen as padding by robotics judges; mitigated by giving it the confirmation and grounding jobs the loop actually needs.
Lower feasibility overall: if the plan accuracy spike fails late, the pivot to concept 1 costs a day.
fallback: Tiered: (1) if plan extraction is unreliable, the robot narrates what it saw per keyframe ('you picked up the red can... you put it in the right tray') and executes only the steps it is sure of, asking for the rest; (2) if that is still shaky, 'Copy me': the judge performs a gesture, Gemma classifies it from 3 frames and the robot mirrors it (ExecuteAction), plus voice Q&A about the table scene; this is reliable and still participatory; (3) if the grasp fails, the robot points at the source tray and target tray in order and narrates, and the gesture step is executed; (4) if the Pi is late, confirmation moves to the arcade button on the Jetson and EmbeddingGemma runs on PC2 CPU via litert-lm serve, keeping the LiteRT story.
angle: Expected-value maximizer: treat the award list as a portfolio. Shared assumptions behind every probability below: ~30 teams (100-120 builders in 3-4s), ~15 in Track 2 with 1-3 humanoids; a humanoid that hears, sees and completes one physical act fully offline is the Track 2 benchmark-beater IF it works on the day, so P(win) = P(works) x P(win | works). Stacking is unstated at AGI House (Kaggle precedent allows it); I weight P(stacking allowed) = 0.6 and show each concept's EV both ways. Hardware-award values used: 2x Pixel 11 ~$1.8k, 5x Pi 5 ~$0.5k, 5x Coralboard ~$0.5k, Qualcomm 1st ~$5.4k / 2nd ~$1.8k in kit value (criteria unknown; VENTUNO Q unobtainable, so I do not bet on it). Side devices are only worth adding where the story needs them, because every extra device lowers P(works) and dilutes the 'robot in front of you' impression. Three concepts span the risk curve: (1) robot-only, lowest variance, Track 2 + LiteRT; (2) Pixel-as-brain, fattest tail via the $15k Best in Show pool; (3) learn-from-watching, highest wow and stage probability, lowest feasibility. All three keep Gemma 4 E2B as the only perception/decision model, use the measured llama.cpp fast path on the Orin for sub-second perception, and run with a human on the R3 remote (L2+B). Numbers from the harness are Mac measurements; Orin numbers are projections until the day-1 spikes land.

name: Fetch: 'Can you get me a drink?' (voice-to-handover butler, fridge door cut)
one_liner: A judge asks the G1 for a drink in any language; Gemma 4 E2B on the robot's Orin hears it, sees the counter, walks there, picks the can from a tray, walks back and hands it over when it sees your hand, with a human-assisted pick as the built-in, honestly labelled fallback.
story: Anyone who has looked after someone after surgery knows the request: 'could you grab me a drink?' This G1 answers it with no cloud and no joystick. One two-billion-parameter model, Gemma 4 E2B, running on the 16 GB Jetson in its chest, does the hearing, the seeing and the deciding. It takes your voice straight in, no speech-to-text module, and answers in your language. Then it looks: one grounded question per camera frame, 'where is the tray?', 'is the can between my fingers?', 'is a hand reaching for it?', each in under a second, and a state machine we can audit turns those answers into steps, a grasp and a handover. We did not teach it to plan the chore; we taught it to answer honestly, and we show you the question, the answer and the milliseconds on the screen as it works. When the pick fails, and tonight it will once, it says so and asks for help instead of pretending. The fridge door is the next skill, not this week's; everything you see today runs on the robot in front of you.
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (2.5 min, repeats per judge wave, survives interruption at any state). 0:00 Robot standing in FSM 500 on a taped 3x3 m mat, LED white (idle); the bench monitor shows the brain view: live 480x336 frame, last question, answer, tool call JSON, latency ms, state. Teammate R1 holds the R3 remote 1.5 m away (L2+B is the e-stop, said out loud to judges). 0:10 PARTICIPATORY: a judge presses the push-to-talk (foot pedal or the phone page on the robot's AP) and asks in their own language 'can you get me the cola?'; LED blue while listening (VAD-chunked clip <= 10 s). 0:12 One request (image + instruction + audio) returns fetch(object='cola') in about 1-2 s on the Orin; the robot confirms in the speaker's language from Piper, LED green. 0:15-0:45 Approach: every ~0.8 s a frame -> box_2d of 'the tray of cans' -> bearing -> LocoClient.Move(0.3, 0, k*bearing) pulses; stops when the box bottom edge crosses the calibrated line (~0.6 m) or the odometry budget is spent; final alignment with one face_target. 0:45-1:15 Pick (locked stand, no stepping): replay the teleop-recorded right-arm reach over rt/arm_sdk to slot A; gate 'Is the red can between the robot's fingers? yes/no' (crop, 280 tokens); BrainCo right hand to 0.7; grasp-detect by finger stall on rt/brainco/right/state plus a second yes/no on the lifted hand. VISIBLE FAILURE-RECOVERY: one slot per wave is deliberately staged askew; the robot retries slot B once, then says 'I could not grab it, could you place it in my hand?' and opens the hand; the judge places it (second participatory moment), the robot closes on the yes gate and continues. 1:15-1:45 Return: odometry heading back to the request pose, then box_2d of 'the person with the raised hand' to fine-align ('please raise your hand' is spoken on the way). 1:45-2:10 Handover: replayed present pose, 'Is a human hand holding the can? yes/no' at 2 Hz, open on yes, retract, 'here you go', LED white. If no hand within 8 s: 'I will hold it until you are ready'. 2:10-2:30 Judge Q&A over the brain view; printed latency and success tables on the bench. STAGE (3 min): same loop with the host wearing the UAC wireless lavalier; the presenter narrates the brain view on the projector; the askew-can retry-then-ask-for-help is planted so the recovery is seen by the room; close on the success table (n, per-stage counts) and the one-sentence design rule: Gemma answers, code sequences.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B IT QAT (unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL GGUF, the mmproj-BF16 that carries both the vision and the gemma4a audio encoders; alias gemma4-e2b) on PC2 (Orin NX 16 GB) through llama-server built with CUDA arch 87: --jinja -np 1 -c 4096 --swa-full --cache-ram 0, chat_template_kwargs enable_thinking=false, temperature 0 top_k 1, cache_prompt true, one warm-up request at boot. Modalities and budgets: (a) intent: image (480x336, 70 tokens) + fixed instruction + input_audio (16 kHz mono WAV, VAD-chunked <= 10 s = <= 250 audio tokens) -> native tool call fetch(object) with one string argument, max_tokens 24, enum-validated client side; (b) navigation: box_2d with assistant prefill and stop ']' (17 output tokens) for a continuous bearing, the most robust format in the harness (100%, no left/right flips); (c) gates: one-word yes/no questions placed after the image (2 output tokens) for can-between-fingers, can-in-hand, hand-on-can, each on a 280-token crop of the hand region because 70 tokens misses objects in clutter; (d) the reply language comes from the model itself ('answer in the speaker's language'), Piper voice picked from a one-word language tag. Expected Orin latencies (projection, to be replaced by Monday's measurements): yes/no 0.3-0.45 s, box prefill 0.65-0.9 s, tool call 0.6-0.85 s plus audio encoding, so a spoken request to the first step in 1-2 s. E4B is swapped in only if Tuesday's 10-utterance-per-language test shows E2B failing a demo language. Why Gemma is essential and not a wrapper: the ears, the eyes and the intent are one 3 GB model that fits beside the robot stack on a 16 GB board; removing it means adding an ASR, a detector and a text LLM and losing the sub-second per-glance loop that makes the closed loop possible.
litert_role: LiteRT-LM 0.18 on PC2 CPU via pip (litert-lm, litert-lm-api, Python 3.10 on Ubuntu 22.04), running EmbeddingGemma 2 (litert-community bundle, ~485 MB) behind litert-lm serve on :9379 /v1/embeddings as the robot's 'pantry memory': during the approach the state machine asks E2B for a <= 12-token caption every 2 s, embeds caption (and the frame itself if serve accepts image parts in Tuesday's curl test) with timestamp and odometry pose, and judges can ask 'what drinks did you see?' or 'where was the cola?' and get a retrieved answer with the frame shown on the brain view. It is additive and off the critical path; LiteRT-LM GPU (WebGPU/Dawn) gets a 1 h attempt with the prebuilt/linux_arm64 LD_LIBRARY_PATH workaround and is otherwise not used. If the serve spike fails outright, LiteRT = none and the slide does not claim it; the Best Use of LiteRT pool is a secondary target that the plan does not depend on.
architecture: Devices: PC2 (Orin NX 16 GB, JetPack 6.2) runs everything in the loop; the MacBook mirrors the brain view to the bench monitor/projector and is the tested fallback inference host over the robot's own USB AP (10.42.0.1) or a 10 m Ethernet cable; a phone on the AP serves only as a PTT button. PC2 processes: llama-server :8080 (E2B + mmproj, ~5-6 GB with CUDA context at -c 4096); skills.py state machine over unitree_sdk2py DDS on eth0 (LocoClient 'sport': GetFsmId==500, Move/SetVelocity, StopMove, Damp; G1ArmActionClient 'arm': ExecuteAction 26/27/99; AudioClient 'voice': TtsMaker/PlayStream/SetVolume/LedControl; rt/arm_sdk LowCmd publisher at 50 Hz with the kNotUsedJoint weight ramp, kp 60/kd 1.5, after ServiceSwitch('g1_arm_example', 0); rt/brainco/right/cmd at 100 Hz and rt/brainco/right/state for stall-based grasp detect; rt/odommodestate for heading and distance budget; rt/lowstate for mode_machine and a fall guard); ears.py (arecord from the ReSpeaker XVF3800 or UAC lavalier, energy/webrtcvad chunking, PTT gate); mouth.py (Piper aarch64 -> 16 kHz mono int16 -> PlayStream in 50 ms chunks, or aplay to the USB speaker; fixed lines pre-synthesized); eyes.py (UVC webcam at 640x480 via OpenCV -> 480x336 JPEG q85, crops at 280 tokens for hand gates); brainview :8000 (SSE page); litert-lm serve :9379 (EmbeddingGemma 2, CPU). Data flow: PTT -> clip -> one request (image, text, audio) -> fetch(object) -> APPROACH (frame -> box_2d -> bearing -> Move pulse, 1 Hz) -> PICK (replayed reach, yes/no gate, hand close, stall + yes/no) -> RETURN (odometry heading + box_2d person) -> HANDOVER (present pose, hand gate at 2 Hz, open) -> idle. Safety invariants in code: arms extend only in locked stand, never while stepping; Move pulses of 1 s with a hard cap of 12 per leg; any gate 'no' twice -> speak and wait; remote holder within 1.5 m; L2+B at any time; never L2+R2 during the day. Expected cycle: 2-2.5 min end to end, of which Gemma compute is about 20 s.

prize_targets: Track 2 Physical AI / IoT / Robotics (1st-3rd): a real humanoid, closed loop on real hardware, all local, Gemma-specific features (native audio-in, 70-token vision, native tool calls) with measured latencies and an honest success table

name: Lead Me: a seeing-eye humanoid guide you can talk to
one_liner: A blindfolded person holds a handle on the G1's forearm and says 'take me to the plant' in any language; Gemma 4 E2B on the Orin hears it, finds the target one grounded glance at a time, walks at their pace, narrates what it sees, stops for anyone who steps in, and remembers what it passed.
story: Guide dogs are scarce, take years to train and cannot tell you what is in front of you. This is a guide you can talk to. Put your hand on its forearm and say where you want to go, in whatever language you speak. One small model, Gemma 4 E2B, running on the Jetson in its chest, takes your voice directly, no speech-to-text in between, and answers you in your language. Then it looks: one honest question per camera frame, 'where is the plant?', 'is the way ahead clear?', each answered in well under a second, and it walks at a human pace, telling you what matters: 'person on your left, two meters'. When someone steps into the path, it stops and says so. When you ask 'did we pass a water fountain?', it checks what it saw on the way and answers. It is not a map and it is not a cloud service; it is a pair of eyes and ears that explain the world and walk beside you. Blindfold one of you and try it, that is the whole demo, and everything that happens runs on the robot in front of you.
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (2-3 min, repeatable, resumable). 0:00 Robot standing in FSM 500 on a taped 4 m course with two distinctive targets (a bright potted plant, an EXIT sign on a stand) and the brain view on the bench monitor. R1 holds the remote within 1.5 m; the walker holds a strap handle on the robot's left forearm (not the hand, so a fall cannot pull a person). 0:10 PARTICIPATORY: a judge (or a teammate if the judge prefers to watch) puts on the sleep mask and presses the PTT on the pedal: 'take me to the plant' in English, Spanish or Mandarin; LED blue. 0:12 One request (image + instruction + audio) -> guide_to(target='plant'); robot confirms in the speaker's language ('ok, the plant, about four meters, walking'), LED green. 0:15-0:50 Guided walk at 0.3 m/s: each cycle (~1 s) a frame -> presence gate yes/no -> box_2d bearing -> Move(0.3, 0, k*bearing); every third cycle a <= 12-token caption spoken ('table on the right'); a 'is anything within two meters directly ahead? yes/no' gate every cycle. VISIBLE FAILURE-RECOVERY: a teammate steps into the path; the robot stops within one pulse, LED orange, 'someone is in the way, waiting', resumes when the gate clears; a second planted case: ask for 'the fridge' which is not in the room and the robot answers 'I cannot see a fridge from here' instead of walking. 0:50 Stop 0.8 m from the target: 'the plant is in front of you, slightly left'. 1:00 Q&A: 'what is around me?' -> Gemma describes the live frame in one sentence -> TTS; 'did we pass a water fountain?' -> EmbeddingGemma 2 retrieval over the route frames -> 'yes, about ten seconds ago on your right' with the retrieved frame shown. 1:30 Second command in another language to the EXIT sign; 2:30 judge reads the printed latency and course-success table. STAGE (3 min): the host or a teammate is blindfolded; three commands in three languages; the planted obstacle; the live scene description; the memory question; close with the numbers slide. Backup video on the MacBook.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B IT QAT (unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL + mmproj-BF16 with the audio encoder) on PC2 through llama-server CUDA arch 87, --jinja -np 1 -c 4096 --swa-full --cache-ram 0, thinking off, greedy, cached system prefix, one warm-up request. Modalities: (a) commands as native audio (16 kHz mono, VAD-chunked <= 10 s, <= 250 audio tokens) with the frame (70 tokens) and a fixed instruction -> native tool call guide_to(target) or describe() with at most one string argument, max_tokens 24, validated client side; the reply language is whatever the model answers in; (b) per-cycle perception on the 480x336 frame: presence gate (one word, 2 tokens, ~0.3-0.45 s on the Orin), box_2d with assistant prefill for the bearing (17 tokens, ~0.65-0.9 s), the clear-ahead gate (one word), and every third cycle a <= 12-token caption for narration; (c) on-demand one-sentence scene description (max_tokens 40, ~1.5 s). Budget per walking cycle about 1.0-1.4 s of Gemma time on the Orin (projection; replaced by Monday's table), matching 1 s Move pulses so the robot never outruns its perception. E4B only if Tuesday's language scoring says so. Why Gemma is essential: the same 3 GB model is the multilingual ears (native audio, no ASR), the eyes (sub-second grounded answers at 70 tokens) and the voice of the explanation; a swap-in text LLM would need an ASR, a detector and a captioner and would not fit beside the robot stack.
litert_role: LiteRT-LM 0.18 on PC2 CPU running EmbeddingGemma 2 behind litert-lm serve :9379 /v1/embeddings as 'route memory': every cycle's caption (plus the image if serve accepts image parts in Tuesday's curl test) is embedded with timestamp and rt/odommodestate pose into an in-process list; a memory question embeds the query and returns the nearest frame, which the robot answers and the brain view shows. Genuinely in the loop (the memory answer is impossible without it), small (485 MB, CPU), off the critical walking path, dropped first if memory is short, and never claimed on the slide if the spike fails. No LiteRT on the Orin GPU beyond a 1 h attempt; no Pi or Pixel side devices.
architecture: Devices: PC2 runs the loop; MacBook mirrors the brain view and is the tested fallback inference host over the robot's own USB AP or Ethernet; a foot pedal (or the phone page on the AP) is the PTT. PC2 processes: llama-server :8080; guide.py state machine over unitree_sdk2py DDS on eth0 (LocoClient: GetFsmId==500, Move(vx, vy, vyaw) 1 s pulses at vx <= 0.3, StopMove, Damp; AudioClient: TtsMaker/PlayStream/LedControl; rt/odommodestate for pose and the distance budget; rt/lowstate fall guard); ears.py (XVF3800 on the chest for the bench, UAC lav for the stage, arecord + VAD, PTT gate); mouth.py (Piper en/es/zh/fr/de voices -> PlayStream 50 ms chunks or the USB speaker; fixed lines pre-synthesized, narration lines synthesized on the fly ~0.2-0.5 s); eyes.py (UVC webcam at the chest, 480x336 JPEG, optional Mid-360 point-cloud minimum range in a 60 degree cone as a second, non-Gemma stop guard if the lidar topic reads cleanly on Tuesday, otherwise step cap only); brainview :8000; litert-lm serve :9379. Data flow per cycle (~1 s): frame -> presence gate -> box_2d -> bearing -> clear-ahead gate -> Move pulse or stop -> every third cycle caption -> TTS, with the memory writer embedding the caption asynchronously. Safety invariants: speed 0.3 m/s, pulses of 1 s, hard cap of 20 pulses per command, stop on gate 'yes', stop on lidar cone < 0.8 m if enabled, handle on the forearm rather than hand-holding, no arm motion while walking, remote holder within 1.5 m, L2+B e-stop announced to every judge.

name: Show Me Once: teach a chore through the robot's own arms, Gemma labels it, anyone runs it by voice
one_liner: A judge puts on the headset and does a 30-second tabletop chore through the G1's arms; Gemma 4 E2B watches the recording and names it; from then on anyone can say the chore in any language and the robot checks the scene, replays the motion and tells you if the world changed.
story: Robots in homes will have to learn chores the way a new roommate does: you show them once. We could not train a policy in a week, so we built the honest version, and it works. You put on the headset and do the chore through the robot's own arms, thirty seconds, done. Gemma 4 E2B, the same two-billion-parameter model running on the Jetson in the robot's chest, watches the recording a frame at a time and writes the label: 'put the marker in the cup', and which objects mattered. From that moment the robot owns the skill. Anyone can ask for it in any language; Gemma hears the request directly, matches it to what it was taught, looks at the table, and only if the marker is where you taught it does it replay the motion. If you moved the cup, it tells you, 'the cup is about twenty centimeters right of where you showed me', instead of flailing. No cloud, no data center, no overnight training: a demonstration, a label, a check and a replay, all auditable on the screen. Teach it something new right now; it will do it for the next judge.
demo_script: BENCH LOOP (3 min per judge wave, resumable; the robot can stay on its stand all day, which is the point). 0:00 Robot in locked stand (FSM 500, on the stand or standing on the mat) at a table with a tray with taped positions; brain view shows the skill library (5 pre-taught cards: stack the cup, hand me the marker, ring the bell, wave the flag, high-five), each with keyframes, label, objects, duration. 0:10 PARTICIPATORY (teach): a judge puts on the Quest (xr_teleoperate --arm G1_23 --ee brainco --record, host on its usual machine, headset on the robot's own AP) and does a 20-30 s chore, coached to move slowly: e.g. move the cup onto the X. 0:45 Ingest: hand-speed keyframes (4-6 frames at 70 tokens each) -> Gemma 'In five words, what did the robot's right hand do?' and 'Which object did it move?' -> a new skill card appears in ~3-5 s on the Orin, with the label editable by voice ('call it the cup thing'). 1:00 PARTICIPATORY (run): a second person presses PTT and says in their language 'do the cup thing' -> run_skill(query) -> EmbeddingGemma 2 retrieval picks the taught skill -> precondition: box_2d of the cup vs its taught start position -> within tolerance -> replay over rt/arm_sdk at 50 Hz with the hand positions replayed at 100 Hz -> postcondition gate 'Is the cup on the X? yes/no' -> 'done, the cup is on the X'. 1:45 VISIBLE FAILURE-RECOVERY: the judge moves the cup 20 cm; same command; the robot says 'the cup is about 20 cm right of where you taught me, put it back or teach me again' and does not move; cup replaced; command repeated; replay succeeds. 2:15 Multilingual run of a pre-taught skill ('dame el marcador' -> hand-me-the-marker with the handover release on the hand gate). 2:45 Judge reads the printed table: skills taught today, runs, successes, refusals. STAGE (3 min): the host teaches a skill live on stage, Gemma labels it on the projector, a second host runs it by voice in another language, the moved-object refusal is shown, the replay succeeds, close with the numbers and the honest sentence: 'taught by demonstration, labelled and checked by Gemma, replayed by code'.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B IT QAT (unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL + mmproj-BF16) on PC2 through llama-server CUDA arch 87, --jinja -np 1 -c 4096 --swa-full --cache-ram 0, thinking off, greedy, cached prefix. Three jobs: (a) labelling a demonstration from video-as-frames: 4-6 hand-speed keyframes at 70 tokens each (<= 420 image tokens) plus two direct questions ('in five words, what did the right hand do?', 'which object did it move?'), max_tokens 20 each, ~2-4 s on the Orin (prefill ~1 s per 420 tokens projected); (b) voice intent: image + instruction + native audio (<= 10 s clip) -> native tool call run_skill(query) or teach(name), one string argument, validated client side; (c) scene checks: box_2d with prefill on a 280-token tabletop crop for the precondition (taught start position vs now, tolerance tuned Tuesday on 30 frames) and one-word yes/no postconditions, 0.3-0.9 s. Why Gemma is essential: the labelling, the multilingual spoken intent and the grounded checks are all one 3 GB model on the board the robot already has, and the honesty of the system (refuse when the scene differs) is a Gemma answer, not a hand-coded threshold on pixels. E4B swapped in only for labelling if Tuesday's scoring shows E2B below 8/10 on labels, since labelling is off the real-time path.
litert_role: LiteRT-LM 0.18 on PC2 CPU serving EmbeddingGemma 2 (/v1/embeddings on :9379) as the skill index: each taught skill's label, object names and (if serve accepts image parts) its first keyframe are embedded; a spoken request's extracted query is embedded and the top-1 skill is retrieved over a library that grows as judges teach. This is the right tool for an open-ended, growing set (no prompt stuffing, no enum to regenerate) and is genuinely in the loop for every run. Fallback if the spike fails: Gemma picks from an enumerated list in the tool schema while the library is small, and LiteRT is not claimed.
architecture: Devices: the teleop host where xr_teleoperate runs today (keep it) with the Quest on the robot's own USB AP; PC2 runs inference, skills, replay, mic, TTS, brain view; the MacBook mirrors the brain view and is the fallback inference host. PC2 processes: llama-server :8080; skills.py (teach: watch the --record episode folder, resample joint states to 50 Hz, clamp joint velocities, extract keyframes by hand speed, call Gemma for the label, store the card as JSON with the start-frame box_2d of the moved object; run: retrieve via litert-lm serve, precondition box_2d on the live crop, interpolate from the current joints to the recorded first frame over 2 s under the kNotUsedJoint weight ramp, replay over rt/arm_sdk at 50 Hz with kp 60/kd 1.5 after ServiceSwitch('g1_arm_example', 0), replay BrainCo finger positions on rt/brainco/{left,right}/cmd at 100 Hz, ramp the weight down, postcondition yes/no, speak); ears.py (XVF3800 / lav, VAD, PTT); mouth.py (Piper -> PlayStream or USB speaker); eyes.py (UVC webcam at the chest, 480x336 for intent, 280-token crops for the table); brainview :8000 with skill cards; litert-lm serve :9379. No locomotion required; the robot can stay on its stand (arms work in locked stand), which removes fall risk and battery anxiety for most of the day; the handover skills run standing on the mat only if Wednesday's standing-replay rehearsal is clean. Expected timings: teach ingest 3-5 s, voice-to-replay-start 1.5-2.5 s, replay 20-30 s, postcondition 0.4 s.
