angle: Learn-from-watching and embodied intelligence, done honestly. The event text asks for "a robot that learns a chore from watching you once" and "sees, hears, reasons and acts"; the Gemma judges reward "disciplined, non-hallucinatory design", auditable reasoning, offline operation and real numbers, and the AGI House robotics crowd discounts teleop. So every concept here separates what is LEARNED in one viewing (the recipe: which objects, which order, which zones, which names, which places) from what is PRE-BUILT (the verbs: parameterized skills with provenance labels: canned Unitree gesture / XR-guided recording / parametric code), shows both on a "robot's mind" screen next to measured latencies, logs an autonomous success-rate table, and keeps the XR headset in a closed box at demo time. Technically all three ride the harness's proven path: never ask E2B to plan from a video (SeeDo showed open VLMs score ~0 at that); ask one direct perception question per keyframe or per frame after the image (222-378 ms on the Mac, projected 0.6-1.2 s on the Orin), feed spoken requests straight into E2B as audio (verified on the Mac, 232-511 ms) emitting <=2-argument tool calls, and let code own sequencing, geometry and the safety envelope. The three concepts are three different learning modes with different risk profiles: (1) Show Once = procedure imitation from the robot's own camera (arms, tabletop); (2) Apprentice = motor skills taught by guiding the robot's hands once via the existing XR teleop, labeled by Gemma from the robot's own video and recalled by voice in any language, with a live teaching moment at the bench (arms, lowest risk because teleop already works on this robot); (3) Show Me Around = a guided tour that becomes a spoken-place map, then one-sentence errands that the robot walks, verifies and reports (legs, continuity with the fetch-a-drink navigation leg). All three share one stack on PC2 (llama.cpp CUDA for Gemma 4 E2B reflexes; LiteRT for MoveNet keyframing and LiteRT-LM for EmbeddingGemma 2 memory; Piper TTS; a USB mic with push-to-talk), so the team can start one and fall back to another without re-platforming. The crucial first-48-hour facts are the same for all three: does Gemma audio run on the Orin under llama.cpp CUDA, does rt/arm_sdk replay hold balance in FSM 500, does LocoClient move on this firmware, and does a USB mic give usable speech in a loud room.

name: Show Me Around (a guided tour becomes a map, then one-sentence errands)
one_liner: Walk the G1 around a space once while naming places; Gemma 4 E2B builds a spoken-place map from your voice and its camera, and afterwards composes multi-step errands from one sentence ('take this to the table, check the fridge, come back'), walking, verifying with its own eyes and reporting, no map file and no operator.
story: The first thing you do with a new helper is show them around: 'this is the fridge, this is the table, this is where I sit.' After that you don't program them, you just ask. This is a Unitree G1 that learns a place the way a person does: once. This morning we walked it around this floor for ninety seconds. I pointed and said 'this is the fridge' in English; my teammate said 'esta es la mesa' in Spanish. Gemma 4, running on the robot's own Jetson with no network, heard the words, named the places, and kept a snapshot of what each one looks like, together with where the robot's legs say it is. Now I hand it a can and say one sentence: 'take this to the table, then check whether the fridge is closed, and come back.' It walks there, finds the person, hands it over when it sees a hand, goes to the fridge, looks, and comes back to tell me. The honest line: what it LEARNED is the map and the names, from one tour; what we BUILT are walk, turn, hand over, look and report, and a safety envelope with a human on the e-stop. And this is the first leg of the chore we are actually building toward: getting a drink from the fridge by itself.
demo_script: BENCH (needs a ~3x3 m clear floor beside the table; if the venue cannot give it, the bench shows the tour and a 1.5 m two-place errand). 0:00 Robot standing; mind screen shows the live head camera, the place map (names, odometry poses, snapshot thumbnails), 'NO DEFAULT ROUTE' badge, run log. 0:10 TOUR (participatory from the start): a judge in the hi-vis teacher vest walks 1.5 m to a mini-fridge prop and says 'this is the fridge' (any language); the robot follows the vest (box_2d bearing and box height from the head camera at ~1 Hz, Move pulses at 0.3 m/s, lidar/depth min-range stop at 0.8 m); when it hears the name, Gemma emits name_place('fridge') and the robot stores odometry pose + snapshot + EmbeddingGemma 2 embedding, says 'Fridge. Got it.' Judge walks to the table: 'this is the table.' 0:50 ERRAND: presenter places a can in the robot's right hand ('hold' -> BrainCo close 0.7), judge speaks one sentence: 'Take this to the table and then check if the fridge is closed.' Screen shows Gemma's tool calls: go_to('table'), hand_over(), go_to('fridge'), check('fridge door closed'), go_to('start'), report(). 1:00 Robot walks to the table pose (odometry), re-verifies the view ('Is this the table I saw? yes' plus the embedding similarity), finds a person (box_2d), faces them, extends the arm, releases when a hand is seen holding the can. 1:30 Walks to the fridge, asks itself 'Is the fridge door closed?' and says the answer, returns to the start pose, reports in the judge's language. 1:50 FAILURE-RECOVERY: at the fridge a teammate stands in the way; the vision check fails ('I can't see the fridge; someone is in front of it'), the robot waits 3 s, re-checks, turns 15 degrees and re-checks, then either continues or reports the failure honestly; a second type: odometry drift puts it 0.3 m off, the snapshot check fails, it turns toward the box_2d bearing of the fridge and corrects. 2:10 Presenter: run log (n errands, completions, interventions), median perception answer ms, 'this is leg one of fetch-a-drink; legs two to four (door, grasp, close) are future work and we say so.' STAGE (2.5 min): 0:00 opener 0:20 60-second tour across the stage with a volunteer naming two places in their language 1:20 one-sentence errand with a hand-over to the volunteer 2:00 the blocked-view recovery 2:20 numbers, no-network screen, honest scope; backup video ready.
gemma_role: Gemma 4 E2B on llama-server CUDA on PC2, thinking off, greedy, same cached GGUF + mmproj. (1) Tour: audio clips (VAD or PTT, <=8 s, 16 kHz mono, placed after the text) -> name_place(name) tool call (1 arg), language detected for later replies; the model also answers 'Describe this place in five words' on the snapshot for the map card. (2) Following: 'Where is the person in the orange vest: left third, center third, right third?' as the face_target call or box_2d with prefill at 480x336 = 70 tokens (the harness's 97-100% path) at ~1 Hz; box height gives a rough range. (3) Errand composition: one spoken sentence -> a sequence of <=2-arg tool calls over the enum of learned places (go_to(place), hand_over(), check(question), report()); the harness showed E2B composes text-to-plan reliably when the rule is in the system prompt and no image is in that turn, so the errand call is text/audio only, and each tool call is validated against the place enum client-side. (4) At each place: yes/no verification questions on the live frame ('Is this the fridge I saw?', 'Is the fridge door closed?', 'Is there a person within two meters?'), person box_2d to face the recipient, the release gate ('Is a human hand holding the can?'). (5) Spoken reports in the requester's language via Piper. Why Gemma is essential: one model hears names in any language, grounds places and people in images, composes the errand and verifies the world at every step; swapping it for an ASR + detector + LLM triple would lose the 'ask the scene a question' loop that makes the recovery honest. Walking, turning, pose bookkeeping and stop distances are code.
litert_role: EmbeddingGemma 2 via litert-lm serve /v1/embeddings (CPU) as the place memory: each named place stores the snapshot's image embedding (and the spoken name's audio/text embedding); at arrival the live frame's embedding is compared to the stored one as a second, cheap relocalization check beside Gemma's yes/no question, and a spoken place name in another language is matched to the stored name by embedding before Gemma confirms. Optional MoveNet (ai-edge-litert) on the teacher's pointing arm to confirm which direction 'this' refers to. This is a modest but genuine LiteRT-LM job; it does not compete with the fast loop. Bonus if LiteRT-LM GPU runs on PC2: the errand-composition call (text only, not latency critical) moves to LiteRT-LM.
architecture: Only PC2 computes. Sensors: D435i RGB via V4L2 (640x480, the head camera is the right viewpoint for following and places), odometry from rt/odommodestate (500 Hz) for place poses and dead reckoning, the Livox Mid-360 cloud (10 Hz, Unitree lidar service topic per 04_06) or D435i depth (pyrealsense2 if the JetPack 6 source build succeeds) for a 0.8 m min-range stop; XVF3800 chest mic (DOA for 'turn toward the speaker') or the judge's lavalier, PTT button for the noisy room. Locomotion: LocoClient in FSM 500 (R1+X): Move(vx, vy, vyaw) pulses (1 s auto-stop is the safety feature) or SetVelocity with duration, vx <= 0.3 m/s, vyaw <= 0.4 rad/s, StopMove on any check failure; a code-side envelope: no motion without a fresh odometry sample, no motion within 0.8 m of an obstacle, max 6 m per leg, the spotter on L2+B. Teaching alternative if following is unreliable: the spotter drives the robot with the R3 remote during the tour (keys readable on rt/wirelesscontroller) while the places are named by voice; execution is autonomous either way and the screen says which one happened. Map: {name, pose(x,y,yaw) from odometry, snapshot jpeg, embedding, language}. Errand executor: state machine with go_to by proportional heading control on odometry, final alignment by the place snapshot check and box_2d bearing of the landmark, hand_over via a recorded rt/arm_sdk extension (G1_23_ArmController) with BrainCo open on the release gate, check() = a Gemma yes/no, report() = Piper over the USB speaker/PlayStream, LEDs via LedControl. Expected latencies (projections): following decision 0.6-1.0 s per frame at 70 tokens; name_place from a 3 s clip 1-1.5 s; errand composition 1.5-2.5 s; each verification 0.6-1.0 s; a 3 m leg at 0.3 m/s ~12 s; whole errand ~60-80 s. Memory: E2B server ~5 GB GPU, EmbeddingGemma 2 ~1 GB CPU. Continuity: the face_target/box_2d bearing code and the bench harness variants are reused as-is; the fridge check is literally the first leg of fetch-a-drink.

angle: Learn-from-watching and embodied intelligence, done honestly. The event text asks for "a robot that learns a chore from watching you once" and "sees, hears, reasons and acts"; the Gemma judges reward "disciplined, non-hallucinatory design", auditable reasoning, offline operation and real numbers, and the AGI House robotics crowd discounts teleop. So every concept here separates what is LEARNED in one viewing (the recipe: which objects, which order, which zones, which names, which places) from what is PRE-BUILT (the verbs: parameterized skills with provenance labels: canned Unitree gesture / XR-guided recording / parametric code), shows both on a "robot's mind" screen next to measured latencies, logs an autonomous success-rate table, and keeps the XR headset in a closed box at demo time. Technically all three ride the harness's proven path: never ask E2B to plan from a video (SeeDo showed open VLMs score ~0 at that); ask one direct perception question per keyframe or per frame after the image (222-378 ms on the Mac, projected 0.6-1.2 s on the Orin), feed spoken requests straight into E2B as audio (verified on the Mac, 232-511 ms) emitting <=2-argument tool calls, and let code own sequencing, geometry and the safety envelope. The three concepts are three different learning modes with different risk profiles: (1) Show Once = procedure imitation from the robot's own camera (arms, tabletop); (2) Apprentice = motor skills taught by guiding the robot's hands once via the existing XR teleop, labeled by Gemma from the robot's own video and recalled by voice in any language, with a live teaching moment at the bench (arms, lowest risk because teleop already works on this robot); (3) Show Me Around = a guided tour that becomes a spoken-place map, then one-sentence errands that the robot walks, verifies and reports (legs, continuity with the fetch-a-drink navigation leg). All three share one stack on PC2 (llama.cpp CUDA for Gemma 4 E2B reflexes; LiteRT for MoveNet keyframing and LiteRT-LM for EmbeddingGemma 2 memory; Piper TTS; a USB mic with push-to-talk), so the team can start one and fall back to another without re-platforming. The crucial first-48-hour facts are the same for all three: does Gemma audio run on the Orin under llama.cpp CUDA, does rt/arm_sdk replay hold balance in FSM 500, does LocoClient move on this firmware, and does a USB mic give usable speech in a loud room.
